content:
Writing #36449, I feel that there should be a way to generate this PR automatically. All I'm doing is checking if e.g. a use of docs#MDifferentiable can be written using the MDiff elaborator and, if so, replacing it. (And doing the same for MDifferentiable{At,On,Withinin}, and similar declarations.) These notations have matching delaborators now (resp. will have them soon). Thus, this PR could also be generated by, for each declaration:

  • printing each hypothesis, and the main goal (making use of currently available notation, including scoped notation)
  • try to elaborate that expression: if not, continue to the next declaration
  • if it does, replacing the declaration with its notation form (and be happy)

@Thomas Murrills is this something Skimmer could do in the future?
@Damiano Testa Or maybe can a linter already do so today?
This check would be rather general (for instance, it would also catch when Topology is opened, but nhds x is written instead of 𝓝 x, etc.) --- but I presume that almost all of these would be desired.
For differential geometry, this would be really nice: as further elaborators are developed, the tool could auto-apply the available fixes --- there is an immediate use case already.
(Though I presume the real strength lies in it applying to any notation!)

This is squarely in scope for skimmer! :) This is a great use case, thanks.

Just to be clear, are you only refactoring type signatures? Or would this ideally apply to any usage of those declarations?

That's great to hear - I really look forward to this being possible! What's the approximate time horizon? (Is there a chance an early version of this could be available soon, in the order of weeks rather than months?)

#36449 illustrates it well: I'd like to cover references in theorem statements (hypotheses and conclusion) for sure. have, suffices etc. would also be nice to have. So, "any usage" is nice, but "only type signatures" would already help a lot.

Hmm, there could be a rudimentary version in weeks, if my suspicions are correct: namely, that we don’t need to replace the whole goal/hypotheses all at once? This notation should elaborate to the same expression as before, right?
Yes, the notation should elaborate to the same expression. (It will not elaborate in 100% of all cases, and that's by design. But elaboration should not change meaning.)

Ok, great! Then maybe a regular linter could simply walk the infotrees and make a try-this suggestion, and then skimmer could apply them. I think this would work for hypotheses, though I’d have to check.
Applying all interactive trythis suggestions is very close at hand; targeted discussion here :)

If you'd like a good testing ground, trying on top of #36318 could be helpful: after that commit, all uses of MDifferentiable{,At,On,WithinAt} have delaborators, so just the linter would cover all applications of these.
